PullRequest.Title: Agent host: New Chat in Worktree starts in the chat area while it replaces the Chat view
PullRequest.Body:
## What

With `chat.editorWindow.enableWorktree` on, **New Chat in Worktree** now also shows while the chat area replaces the Chat view (`chat.viewSessions.openInChatPart`), and starts the worktree chat there with the local agent host. Otherwise it opens in the Chat view, as before. Where the folder cannot have a new worktree (not Git, or no HEAD), the chat area refuses like the Chat view: it warns and the draft is not sent in the folder.

## Changes

- `agentHostNewChatActions.ts`: drops the `chatPartEnabled` check. While a host replaces the Chat view, `run` asks it for `{ folder, providerId: 'local-agent-host', sessionType: 'copilotcli', placement: 'worktree' }`; if the host declines, the existing Chat view path prepares the worktree chat.
- `newChatWidget.ts`: when the requested draft cannot work in a new worktree, it warns once and keeps send disabled; it still applies New Worktree if that becomes available, and picking another workspace clears it.
- `LOCAL_AGENT_HOST_PROVIDER_ID` moves to `platform/agentHost/common/agentHostConnectionsService.ts`, so chat can name the provider; `agentHostSessionsProvider.ts` re-exports it.
- Windows-path tests for F4 (G1–G4): Worktrees filter labels at drive roots; the folder follow with drive-letter case, a chat on another drive or a share, and terminal marks.

## Notes for reviewers

- The host is asked without `ownChat`, so a decline is not turned into a default Chat view chat that skips the worktree.
- Provider and session type are pinned, since the chat area otherwise starts the user's last-picked agent.
- Only this action requests `placement: 'worktree'`, so the refusal does not affect other composers or the send-time worktree question.
- Windows unit tests for PRs into `main` run only in the merge queue.

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run oxlint <changed files>`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run newChatWidget, agentHostNewChatActions, agentsChatViewHost tests`: 327 passing (the refusal test fails without the fix)
- `./scripts/test.sh --run sessionWorktreeFolders, agentHostWorktree, agentHostNewChatActions tests`: 39 passing
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium --run <same>`: 38 passing

Follows #348306 (merged).

Scenarios.Scenario: New Chat in Worktree is accepted by the replacement chat-area host.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action awaits opening one composer. Draft creation and configuration resolve asynchronously; usable configuration and the requested isolation must settle before sending. Initial configuration reaches the agent host, Copilot managed-settings RPC, and Git isolation probes. Branch loading and eager provisional-backend creation are existing draft initialization, not an added collection-wide preparation step.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve draft schema/values through connection.resolveSessionConfig; apply requested worktree isolation through the existing configuration-write path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One draft: one discovery request, optionally one initial-value reconciliation request, and at most one placement-triggered refresh when isolation changes. Further calls require existing configuration/provider events or user actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This action prepared sidebar configuration through AgentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService, normally one successful preparation request plus existing picker initialization. The replacement-host route is new; the provider configuration machinery itself is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Configuration availability gates sending, but the action opens the composer without first waiting for the old sidebar preparation timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe repository root, HEAD, and default branch using existing Git commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected folder per effective configuration resolution. Concurrent same-folder Git-info reads share one request; warm successful root lookups avoid another rev-parse. HEAD/default-branch probes are refreshed after prior requests settle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Sidebar preparation also called resolveSessionConfig, which uses the same host-owned isolation contribution and Git probes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Contributes to configuration readiness, as it already did for preparing a worktree chat before this PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ensure the existing SDK client and resolve organization-managed settings through managedSettings.resolve.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One effective managed-settings query per RPC/token/folder while pending; sequential resolutions can query again. This diff adds no per-session-history or per-ref RPC fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Copilot configuration resolver was reached by sidebar worktree preparation. SDK startup and managed-settings resolution are not new underlying boundaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of configuration readiness; runtime-internal network duration is opaque to this repository-level review.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load branch completions and create/subscribe to one provisional backend for the visible draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one guarded eager-create task per draft; one coalesced branch load with nonempty results retained. Branch completions use the existing bounded set of Git queries whose returned data scales with refs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The action used the sidebar's existing provisional-session/picker path. Routing to the chat area newly selects this existing draft initializer; it does not add hidden composers or duplicate drafts in a loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing visible-composer initialization; branch loading follows initial configuration. Backend creation is asynchronous rather than awaited by the new action.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicit command, one selected workspace folder, and one requested local provider/session type. Git branch-list response size depends on repository refs, not session-history length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The host service supersedes older requests. Within a draft, configuration operations wait for outstanding resolution; backend eager creation is guarded against duplication. Provider configuration and host isolation probing run concurrently. Git HEAD/default-branch queries run concurrently after repository-root resolution. There is no new loop over sessions, folders, or providers issuing boundary requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Draft configuration reads return the existing NewSession config. Initial resolution uses one discovery request and optionally a second request to apply differing initial values; selecting worktree can add one configuration refresh if isolation differs. Branch loading shares an in-flight promise and retains nonempty results per draft. Git-info requests coalesce while pending; successful repository-root lookups use an existing bounded LRU. Copilot managed-settings requests coalesce per RPC instance/token/folder while pending; completed-result freshness remains runtime-owned.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the traced command-to-composer/configuration path and effective one-folder cardinality. The changed code adds a user-requested route, not a demonstrated repeated-work or fan-out regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured timings. SDK-internal caching/network behavior, repository size, and cold-start duration are unknown; none establishes a harmful changed scaling mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: existing draft initialization is reached once for an explicitly requested composer, with existing coalescing and no new collection multiplier.

Scenarios.Scenario: No replacement host exists, or the replacement host declines New Chat in Worktree.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Absent a replacement, execution immediately follows the existing prepareNewAgentHostChat path. A declining AgentsChatViewHost returns before opening a composer; the action then prepares configuration and opens the sidebar chat. The existing overall configuration wait is bounded at 10 seconds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve initial sidebar session configuration through the agent-host connection before opening the prepared chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one successful preparation request for one resource; existing connection-change events can retry until completion or timeout. A normal host decline adds no SDK/Git/configuration call of its own.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The action always used this preparation and sidebar-open path. The path, timeout, transitive Git/managed-settings boundaries, and cleanup remain unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Preparation remains before sidebar opening, as before; the new decline check is local and does not add a remote preparation stage.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One invocation and one untitled sidebar resource; retry frequency follows existing session-resolution changes, not collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One host attempt followed by one sidebar attempt, not simultaneous successful starts. Omitting ownChat prevents ChatViewHostService from also issuing its default-sidebar fallback. Preparation listeners and cancellation are disposed on completion/timeout.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful prepared config is cached for the resource and checked against connection, working directory, and initial values. Failed or unavailable configuration may be retried on existing connection-resolution events. The PR does not change those cache or retry rules.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: host rejection occurs before openComposer, the service fallback is gated by ownChat, and existing preparation/cleanup code is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Connection startup and configuration duration are environment-dependent; no new slow boundary was identified on the decline path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression found; the old path is preserved without a duplicate default-chat preparation.

Scenarios.Scenario: A requested worktree draft cannot support worktree isolation, then receives config changes, becomes eligible, or the user selects another workspace.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The warning is emitted once and sending intentionally stays disabled until placement can be applied or workspace selection clears the request. This is a behavioral refusal, not an introduced expensive asynchronous wait or polling loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Only if availability later becomes true, apply worktree isolation through provider.setSessionConfigValue and its existing config-resolution RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero additional RPCs while unavailable; at most one placement write after eligibility changes because pending state is cleared first. Repeated unavailable config events do not issue boundary requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The request was cleared after warning, so it could not later apply placement. This PR retains one bounded request to apply once on subsequent availability; initially available placement already used the same write path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Successful placement uses the same existing asynchronous config write as an initially available draft. While unavailable, the disabled send state is intentional and performs no background boundary work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One pending placement object per widget, containing a folder URI, draft identifiers, and one Boolean. Re-evaluation follows existing session/provider/configuration events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new timer, task queue, subscription, or retry request is installed. On availability, pending state is cleared before a single setSelected(true) call. User workspace selection clears the state.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: unavailableReported suppresses repeated warnings. Availability checks read the existing draft/config cache through NewWorktreeChoice; getSessionConfig returns NewSession config directly for these drafts, without subscribing to running sessions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all pending-placement consumers and the draft config getters were inspected; retained state is bounded and passive, not a session/resource graph or repeated-I/O owner.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frequency of later eligibility changes is unknown but cannot multiply the placement write beyond one per retained request.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. Retaining one small placement object and gating send do not establish memory growth, polling, or repeated expensive work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Windows drive/share worktree behavior and local-provider identifier relocation.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Windows changes are test-only. Moving and re-exporting the provider identifier does not change runtime worktree traversal, filtering, or terminal marking.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing folder/worktree lists and path depth; the diff only adds coverage for drive roots, drive-letter case, other drives, and shares.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No production scheduling, concurrency, or lifecycle changes in these areas.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No production cache changes; the identifier remains the same string.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all eight changed-file patches were read completely; these hunks either add tests or relocate a constant.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No runtime performance measurements; no changed cost mechanism was identified.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable production performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix in these hunks.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across the complete eight-file inventory and every diff page. Traced replacement-host routing, sidebar fallback, pending-placement lifecycle, draft configuration, SDK managed-settings RPC, Git probes, branch-load coalescing, and eager backend initialization. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression found; no qualifying regression-fix provenance signal. Static review only; SDK-internal network behavior and measured durations remain unverified.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
